business_problem: Surescripts needed to retire fragile replicated on-premises databases and physical data centers while preserving ultra-high uptime across healthcare transaction processing and accelerating analytics modernization.
solution_summary: Surescripts uses Google Cloud to address this challenge: Surescripts needed to retire fragile replicated on-premises databases and physical data centers while preserving ultra-high uptime across healthcare transaction processing and accelerating analytics modernization. AlloyDB for PostgreSQL backs core transactional records with managed high availability, read scaling, and lower-latency query performance for patient-matching workloads, serving as the storage layer. BigQuery absorbs analytics, legacy Hadoop applications, and OLAP workloads as part of the data lake transformation, serving as the storage layer. Google Kubernetes Engine runs the core transactional microservices after the migration off physical data centers, serving as the orchestration layer. Legacy analytics and OLAP data is shifted into BigQuery, transactional services move onto GKE, and AlloyDB becomes the managed relational core for operational records and the Master Patient Index workload.

Surescripts migrated 30.5B annual transactions off legacy on-premises hardware to AlloyDB, boosting application deployment velocity while safeguarding a 99.998% network uptime mandate.

, the nation’s leading health intelligence platform, serves as a critical connection point linking pharmacies, pharmacy benefit managers, health plans, life sciences companies and health systems across the United States. Processing 30.5 billion transactions annually, the platform operates under a strict availability model where routine maintenance windows or unexpected service outages are unacceptable. Historically, Surescripts managed its high-throughput operational workloads across three secure, on-premises data centers anchored by traditional OLTP infrastructure. However, to accelerate digital transformation, eliminate physical hardware procurement delays, and mitigate catastrophic data center risk, the company launched a comprehensive multi-year modernization strategy to transition their production workloads directly into Google Cloud.
